newsitem.title: UK: Wall Street's firm start boosts European bourses.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street's firm start boosts European bourses.

text.p: European bourses turned modestly higher on Tuesday afternoon after Wall Street defied predictions of a weak start and resumed its heady rally.
The region's three biggest stock markets, London, Paris and Frankfurt, all rose despite their lingering worries about the resilience of U.S. markets.
Unexpectedly weak U.S. housing starts data for October helped Wall Street ignore predictions of more weakness after it closed a point down on Monday following eight record sessions.
By 1530 GMT the Dow Industrials Average was showing a rise of nearly 22 points.
On foreign exchange markets the dollar was marginally softer against the mark and yen, with the spotlight fixed on the buoyant British pound.
Sterling powered to a four-year high of 1.6765 against the dollar. By 1530 GMT the pound was trading just under its highs.
Traders said the dollar remained underpinned against the mark after Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said the central bank would welcome a more stable and stronger dollar.
Germany's blue-chip DAX index closed fractionally higher as Deutsche Telekom joined the 30-share index the day after its scorching global debut with a weighting of 4.5 percent.
Europe's biggest phone company Deutsche Telekom lost ground after Monday's debut, however. It closed floor trade in Frankfurt at 32.07 marks, five percent down from its opening level of 32.20.

The volume of Telekom shares traded was bigger than a normal day's trading in all the DAX 30 shares combined, with over 11 million changing hands in bourse dealings and almost 15 million in computer trade.
"Big and small investors are cashing in," said one trader.
London stocks inched higher through the afternoon after languishing for most of the early session on concerns about Wall Street and next week's British budget presentation.
"There is a nervous stillness occupying this market. We are sandwiched between our own budget and a slight disquiet about what Wall Street might be capable of doing," one trader said.
The FTSE 100 index was up 9.5 points at 3,971.6 around 1530 GMT but volume was thin.
"We need very big stories indeed to break the market out of this mood...and I can't see that happening," a dealer said.

British Gas headed the list of most-traded stocks, with over 21 million shares traded. The shares, which surged on Monday on reports Shell had approached British Gas with a merger proposal, were up 2-1/2p at 231p but well off their highs following a bout of profit-taking.
French shares were only marginally up after earlier gaining a little following the U.S. housing data. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.88 points at 2,229 at 1530 GMT.
Eurotunnel was down 1.92 percent at 7.65 francs but off its lows after a fire in the Channel Tunnel between France and Britain forced the temporary closure of the rail link.
Euro Disney fell 2.18 percent to 11.20 francs after the Paris theme park operator reported a 77 percent rise in 1995-96 profits but said it still faced a tough year.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.37 yen and 1.5024 marks, compared with 111.29 yen and 1.4996 marks in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 9.5 points at 3,971.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 0.09 of a point at 2,228.90.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 0.25 points at 2,764.09. In later screen-based trading the IBIS DAX was up 4.01 points at 2,772.91.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $378.20 against $378.30 in the morning and $379.10 on Monday afternoon. Silver was off one cent at $4.89.
